samples.summary: New source-side refusal branch (merge only partially inside the copied range) has no test
samples.evidence: paste() gains an early `return false` when a merge read live at paste time is not fully contained in `copyBuffer.sourceRange` (sheet.ts:2216-2218). Every merge test in the new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block copies a selection that fully contains the merge (merge.test.ts:94-370); the refusals that ARE tested (merge.test.ts:172, 196, 241, 342) all trip the *destination* check at sheet.ts:2286, not this one. The branch is reachable because the source layout is read at paste time — e.g. copy A1:B1, then merge B1:C1, then paste — but no test constructs that sequence, so a regression that silently drops or inverts this guard (creating a merge wider than the copied content) would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: View-layer change (clear copy buffer only when paste returns true) is untested
samples.evidence: Both spreadsheet.ts:712-717 and worksheet.ts:4896-4901 now gate `clearCopyBuffer()` on the paste return value — the user-visible 'marching ants survive a refused paste' behavior. The new tests only assert the model-level return (`expect(await sheet.paste({text})).toBe(false)`, merge.test.ts:211) and `sheet.isCutMode()`; no test in packages/sheets/test/view/* exercises the paste handler of either view. Searched test/view/*.ts for clearCopyBuffer/paste — no matches.

samples.summary: No test asserts paste() returns true on a successful paste, which is what the views now rely on
samples.evidence: The new contract is 'returns whether the paste was applied' and both view call sites clear the buffer only on `true`. The tests assert `false` twice (merge.test.ts:211, 254) but every success-path test discards the return value (`await sheet.paste({ text })` at lines 104, 125, 141, 165, 187, 234, 276, 301, 319, 335, 364). If paste returned a falsy value on success the whole suite would still pass while the copy buffer/marching ants leaked in the UI.

samples.summary: Cut-source merge exemption (cutAnchors) and overlapping cut-paste onto its own merge are untested
samples.evidence: `cutMerges`/`cutAnchors` (sheet.ts:2262-2267) exempt blocks inside the cut source from the destination refusal check, so an overlapping cut-paste (e.g. cut merged A1:B1 and paste at B1) exercises a path none of the tests hit — the only cut-paste merge test (merge.test.ts:131) moves the block to a non-overlapping row 3, where the exemption never matters. The `isRangeInRange(m.range, cutSourceRange)` filter is likewise never exercised with a partially-contained block.

samples.summary: Extracted clearCellsUnderMerge's spill-anchor / spill-blocked / style-preserving branches have no test on either call path
samples.evidence: clearCellsUnderMerge (sheet.ts:911-957) keeps ghost-cell, spill-anchor cleanup and 'preserve style, delete value' branches. merge.test.ts contains zero occurrences of 'spill' (grep count = 0) and no test asserts that a style survives on a cell cleared under a newly created merge, on either the paste path or the moveRangeTo path. The code is relocated rather than new, but the refactor now shares it between two callers with no coverage of those branches from the new caller.

finding.summary: New source-side refusal branch (merge only partially inside the copied range) has no test
finding.evidence: paste() gains an early `return false` when a merge read live at paste time is not fully contained in `copyBuffer.sourceRange` (sheet.ts:2216-2218). Every merge test in the new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block copies a selection that fully contains the merge (merge.test.ts:94-370); the refusals that ARE tested (merge.test.ts:172, 196, 241, 342) all trip the *destination* check at sheet.ts:2286, not this one. The branch is reachable because the source layout is read at paste time — e.g. copy A1:B1, then merge B1:C1, then paste — but no test constructs that sequence, so a regression that silently drops or inverts this guard (creating a merge wider than the copied content) would go unnoticed.

verdict.reason: The source-side refusal branch is real and reachable: sheet.ts:2204 reads the source merge layout live at paste time and sheet.ts:2216-2218 returns false when a merge is only partially inside copyBuffer.sourceRange, which can happen if a merge is created or widened between copy and paste (e.g. copy A1:B1, merge B1:C1, paste). No test exercises it. I searched repo-wide: only merge.test.ts, clipboard.test.ts and pivot-protection.test.ts call .paste(), and only merge.test.ts combines merges with paste (clipboard.test.ts contains no occurrence of 'merge'; pivot-protection's paste returns early on the pivot guard at sheet.ts:2173; frontend tests never touch merges). In every test of the Sheet merge + copy-paste block the copy source either contains no merge (merge.test.ts:172-194, 196-215, 307-324) or fully contains it (94-112, 114-129, 131-148, 265-281), so getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange) is either empty or fully contained and the guard's predicate is never true. The asserted refusals at merge.test.ts:187, 211, 254 and 351 trip the destination check at sheet.ts:2286 or the external-paste path instead. The nearest test, merge.test.ts:217-239, exercises the live read with an EMPTY copiedMerges list, so it passes vacuously through the some(...) predicate and would still pass with lines 2216-2218 deleted. Deleting or inverting the guard — which would create a destination merge wider than the copied content — is therefore invisible to the suite. Major under the missing-tests rubric: a distinct refusal behavior with data-corrupting consequences and no meaningful coverage.
